parsed.why: No criminalisation; 2019 statute explicitly protecting gender identity; no documented LGBT-specific abuses; openly active queer resident. Thin-data but positive signals and functioning institutions point above midpoint.

Enforced morality policing historically targeted trans people; even after 2022 court strike-down, official discrimination persists; criminalised same-sex conduct enforced; state censorship and documented prosecutions. High-risk band.

Documented societal hostility with thin recourse: legislators' death threats against a trans woman, arson, extortion, 5/100 acceptance, police slow/absent response, no anti-discrimination protection. No criminal statute prevents the worst tier.

Decriminalised, 2024 hate-crime statute explicitly covering gender identity with enhanced penalties, constitutional protections; no documented enforcement or visitor-facing exposures; no same-sex recognition is resident-facing only.

No criminalisation, hate-speech crime, conversion ban, civil unions, accepted SOGIESC recommendations; but inconsistent enforcement — uninvestigated attacks, clergy impunity — and pending gender-recognition law hold it below full Low Risk.
